name: Freedom in the World

govt_response.title: MEA/government reaction to Freedom House 'Partly Free' (2021)
govt_response.summary: Press reports on the government's response to 2021 downgrades; exact MEA wording not retrieved. Treat as unconfirmed.

methodology_note:
'year' is the edition year (covers the prior calendar year). Status fell from Free to Partly Free in the 2021 edition. Edition pages for 2014-2016 were not retrievable (404) and pre-2017 scores are not given on the same 100-point basis here, so those years are omitted. Freedom House pages show a 'Global Freedom Score' of 62 in the sidebar for the latest edition (2026) and also 63 for 2025 in one extract; edition headline scores are used.

Back-fill (pre-2014 editions, researched by deepseek, unreviewed): 'year' is the edition year (covers the prior calendar year). Status fell from Free to Partly Free in the 2021 edition. Freedom House introduced the 0-100 aggregate score with the 2006 edition; earlier editions used only the 1-7 Political Rights and Civil Liberties ratings, so pre-2006 editions are not on a comparable basis and are omitted. The 2014-2016 edition pages were recovered from Internet Archive captures of Freedom House's country pages: 2016 states an Aggregate Score of 77 directly, while for 2014 and 2015 the total is the sum of the published PR and CL sub-scores (2014: PR 34/40 + CL 43/60 = 77; 2015: PR 35/40 + CL 43/60 = 78). Aggregate scores for 2006-2013 could not be confirmed from a retrievable Freedom House page (the archived pre-2016 pages display only 1-7 ratings/status), so those years remain gaps; no value was guessed. Freedom House also revised some indicator rules in 2018 (outside the 2004-2014 window). Freedom House pages show a 'Global Freedom Score' of 62 in the sidebar for the latest edition (2026) and also 63 for 2025 in one extract; edition headline scores are used.
